page.overview:
What is National Pokédex?

The National Pokédex is a type of Pokédex that lists every Pokémon existing at the time the media was released. It appears in the form of an upgrade to regional Pokédex known as National Mode. It orders the Pokémon according to how they were released, following a more chronological order. It was first introduced in , although with more distinct definitions of an Old Pokédex Mode, which refers to the Kanto Pokédex, and a New Pokédex Mode, referring to the Pokémon of the Johto region. The term "National Pokédex" was first introduced in the Generation III games, . A separate diploma is often rewarded for completing the National Pokédex, like with the regional Pokédex.

With the increasingly large number of Pokémon introduced, the National Pokédex would begin to appear irregularly as of Generation VII, in favor of Pokémon Bank or, from onwards, Pokémon HOME. In the case of , the National Pokédex does not appear because it features only the 151 Pokémon from Generation I, as well as Meltan and Melmetal.

In , the Hoenn Pokédex upgrades to the National Pokédex automatically when trading Pokémon from . This is also the case for , even if the Pokémon being traded is part of the Hoenn Pokédex.

In , to receive the National Pokédex, the player needs to have defeated the Elite Four and Pokémon Champion as well as have caught at least 60 Pokémon. Once these conditions have been met, the player can talk to Professor Oak in his laboratory to receive it.
